title: GPU OOM & CUDA driver/library mismatch - scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Running local repro of model-serving inference (llama-7b-like) on dev box (single NVIDIA GPU). Quick notes while debugging; messy.
- Container: ubuntu:22.04 + python 3.10. Using Docker with nvidia runtime / NVIDIA Container Toolkit.
- PyTorch wheel built from upstream nightly (matching instructions in infra README).

Observed failures / symptoms:
- Intermittent CUDA OOMs during warmup or long sequences. Sometimes fails immediately, sometimes after a few requests.
- Occasional driver/runtime mismatch errors when swapping containers or after system driver update.

Commands I ran (sequentially / experiments):
- nvidia-smi\  -> shows driver + processes\  (example output I saw):
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12    Driver Version: 525.85.12    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

- docker run --gpus all -it --rm --env NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 --shm-size=1g my-image /bin/bash
- inside container: python -c \"import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available()); print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())\"
  -> torch.cuda.is_available() = True
  -> torch.version.cuda = '11.7'  
  -> memory_summary shows lots of reserved memory even before workload (fragmentation suspicion).

- Check driver vs runtime: saw message in some runs: \"CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version\" and at other times: \"The NVIDIA driver on your system is too old (required >= 11.7, found 11.4)\".
- Other error seen when driver missing: \"NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver.\" 

Real error snippets (copied from logs):
- RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 312.00 MiB (GPU 0; 10.76 GiB total capacity; 9.50 GiB already allocated; 121.25 MiB free; 1.23 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
- RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory
- RuntimeError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered (when OOM + fragmentation)
- ImportError: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
- libcudnn.so.8: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
- cudaErrorIllegalAddress: an illegal memory access was encountered
- Warning: CUDA runtime version (11.7) does not match CUDA driver version (11.4)

Hypotheses / notes:
- Memory fragmentation / reserved memory from previous allocations (torch caching allocator) causing later small OOMs.
- In some cases not a true capacity OOM but illegal address caused by driver/library mismatch (libcuda/cudnn mismatch) -> shows up as segfault/illegal memory instead of neat OOM.
- Containers using a different CUDA runtime than host driver -> version mismatch errors. Need to align container CUDA toolkit + driver compatibility.
- Shared /dev/shm too small causing unexpected allocation failures for shared buffers (we saw smaller shm).
- Pinned memory / host allocation leak (pinned allocations not freed).
- Batch size + sequence length growth (kv cache) pushes memory slowly until reserved limit.

What I've tried (and outcomes):
1) torch.cuda.empty_cache() between requests in worker - reduced frequency of OOM but not a fix.
2) Set environment: PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128  -> reduced fragmentation in local tests; batch size=2 became stable.
3) Restarting nvidia-persistenced and container: sometimes fixes IllegalAddress until next run.
4) Rebuilt container to use cu102/cu11x wheel variants (experimented). If torch built against 11.7 but host driver is older -> warning + instability.
5) Upgraded host driver (on dev box) to 525.x -> seemed to eliminate driver mismatch warnings. Tests after upgrade show torch.version.cuda still 11.7 but host driver reports compatible.
6) Reduced model seq_len from 2048 to 1024 -> fewer OOMs.
7) Added --shm-size=8g to docker run -> slight improvement for large-batch preprocessing buffer allocations.
8) Switched to torch.compile(False) when using TorchInductor -> reduced illegal memory errors (hypothesis: compiler/runtime combos exposing driver issue).

Experiment notes (detailed):
- When I saw 'libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file' inside container, I confirmed host has /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 and the container did not mount /usr/lib/. Fixed by making sure nvidia-container-runtime mounts driver libs (nvidia/ container toolkit config).
- For mismatch: host driver 510.x + container CUDA runtime 11.7 -> messages. Upgrading driver to 525.x fixed the explicit mismatch messages.
- CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES behavior: when container passed GPUs by index, sometimes process list in nvidia-smi shows other processes occupying GPU memory (unexpected) -> double-check environment variables and cgroup device isolation.

Repro recipe (local) that reliably triggers OOM:
- Model: quantized 7b-ish, sequence length 2048, batch size 2, kv-cache enabled.
- Start container without PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF and small shm. Send two parallel requests that both allocate large outputs -> immediate OOM in one worker.
- Setting max_split_size_mb:128 prevents fragmentation and allows both to succeed (on 12GB GPU).

Next steps / TODOs:
- Re-run full repro on a clean AMI with driver 525.* + matching NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Log exact driver/runtime versions.
- Add a small repro script to repo under ci/repro/gpu_oom_repro.py that spawns parallel inference requests and prints memory_summary before/after.
- Add a pre-start check in container entrypoint to validate libcuda presence and driver compatibility (e.g., compare torch.version.cuda to host driver reported CUDA via nvidia-smi). Fail early with actionable message.
- Try upgrading/downgrading cuDNN to match PyTorch ABI when we hit missing libcudnn errors.
- Investigate switching to torch.multiprocessing.spawn with 'forkserver' to avoid memory copy-on-write surprises.
- Instrument our worker to call torch.cuda.memory_stats() and log reserved/active numbers on failure.

Random breadcrumbs / useful commands I used: 
- nvidia-smi\-q -d MEMORY
- docker run --gpus all --shm-size=8g -e PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 my-image
- python - <<PY
import torch
print(torch.cuda.is_available())
print(torch.version.cuda)
print(torch.cuda.memory_reserved())
print(torch.cuda.memory_allocated())
PY
- ldd $(python -c \"import torch;print(torch._C.__file__)\") | grep cuda
- sudo apt-get install --reinstall nvidia-driver-525
- sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && sudo systemctl restart docker

Open questions for infra/product: 
- For Dedicated capacity machines, should we pin a minimum driver version/AMI across fleet to reduce mismatch problems? Probably yes.
- Do we want to include a debug endpoint that returns GPU memory summary for OBS/Console? (useful for customer debugging).

Notes to self: keep this messy. When filing a proper postmortem or runbook, move all stable repro steps + exact versions to infra/wiki.

End of scratchpad (will update after repro on clean AMI).
